edits.match: The tongue forms early, in the fifth week of embryonic life, when paired lingual swellings appear on the right and left sides of the first pharyngeal arch.
edits.replacement: The tongue forms early, at about the fourth week of development, when paired lateral lingual swellings and a midline swelling, the tuberculum impar, appear on the first pharyngeal arch.
edits.reason: WRONG: StatPearls (Anatomy, Head and Neck, Tongue; Embryology, Tongue) places the start of tongue development at approximately four weeks of gestation with two lateral swellings and the tuberculum impar; 'fifth week' and omission of the tuberculum impar misstate the source.
WRONG: states 'in the fifth week'; the source says approximately four weeks.

notes: SUPPORTED: anterior two-thirds from fused lateral swellings (CN V3 sensation), posterior third from later arches (CN IX). GENERAL KNOWLEDGE (correct): genioglossus protrusion/jaw-thrust, hyoglossus depression/retraction, intrinsic muscles, four papilla types (filiform without taste buds; circumvallate in V-row anterior to sulcus terminalis), chorda tympani taste anterior two-thirds, glossopharyngeal posterior third, hypoglossal motor with deviation towards weak side, lingual artery, taste-cell turnover ~10-14 days (OpenStax), lingual lipase activated in stomach. Clinical text matches NHS mouth cancer / tongue-tie pages. Structures valid; references https on approved hosts.
